Our Story

In Loving Memory of Shaun Duvall

A life defined by faith, love, and quiet service to others.

Shaun's Story

Shaun Duvall was a servant leader — not because of a title, but because of how he lived. As a devoted husband, father, friend, and business owner, he showed up for people. He listened before he led. He wanted to know someone's story and their why, noticed potential in people others overlooked, loved championing the underdog, and was energized by helping someone receive an opportunity they might not otherwise have had.

If Shaun could help, he did. If he couldn't, he tried to connect that person with someone who could. Whether he was in a business meeting, sharing a meal, or mentoring someone, Shaun consistently pointed things back to God — praying with people and over people, wanting God, not himself, to receive the glory.

On Easter Sunday, 2026, Shaun went home to be with the Lord. It was a loss that shook everyone who knew and loved him. [Placeholder — the family is warmly invited to add more here: memories, photos, and the details of Shaun's life that belong to you to share.]

Scriptural Foundation

Romans 5:3–5 has long been a family verse, and it now provides a meaningful framework for the Foundation: difficult circumstances do not have to have the final word. God can work through suffering to produce perseverance, character, and hope. 2 Corinthians 1:4 adds another dimension — the comfort we receive in suffering can equip us to comfort and serve others.

Suffering → Perseverance → Character → Hope

Romans 5:3–5

The Foundation will not be defined by how Shaun died. It will tell people how Shaun lived — and demonstrate that profound loss can be turned outward into hope, service, relationship, and opportunity.

If you or someone you love is walking through a difficult season, you don't have to carry it alone. The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline is available any time, day or night — call or text 988.

"We don't want to preserve Shaun's legacy. We want to multiply it. This Foundation is being built to carry forward the Christ-centered servant leadership Shaun modeled: seeing people, hearing their story and their why, believing in potential, creating meaningful connections, showing up, serving, and helping others find their way. Shaun's life is the inspiration for this work, but God is its foundation."

A Founder's Declaration
Leadership

Our Board & Family

The Foundation is founder-led and mission-protected: the Founder/President stewards the founding vision, while the board provides governance, accountability, community relationships, and shared responsibility.

Cascea Duvall

Founder & President

Cascea founded the Shaun Duvall Legacy Foundation with a simple hope: that the way Shaun loved, served, led, and invested in people would not end with his life, but be a positive lasting impact through the lives of others.

An entrepreneur and business owner for more than two decades, Cascea has spent much of her career leading, mentoring, and helping others grow. Her faith and life experiences have shaped a deep belief that relationships matter more than numbers and that one intentional investment in a person can create an impact far beyond what we may ever see.

As Founder and President, Cascea is committed to carrying that vision forward by investing in young servant leaders and entrepreneurs, challenging them to do the same for someone else.

Carrie Ann (Duvall) Newell

Founding Director & Vice President

Carrie helped establish the Shaun Duvall Legacy Foundation with a deeply personal purpose: to honor her brother Shaun by continuing the legacy of faith, kindness, generosity, and servant leadership that defined his life. As Shaun's sister, Carrie had the privilege of seeing firsthand the way he loved people, believed in others, and used his life and his success to make a difference. Shaun never measured his impact simply by what he accomplished, but by the lives he touched and the people he helped become better, stronger, and more confident in their own purpose.

Carrie brings her own passion for serving others, along with a career dedicated to caring for and advocating for people. Her faith in Jesus and her love for her brother inspire her commitment to ensuring Shaun's legacy continues to reach others.

As Founding Director and Vice President, Carrie is committed to keeping Shaun's story alive — not simply by remembering who he was, but by living out what he believed: that we are called to love others well, serve selflessly, invest in people, and leave the world better than we found it.

Dan Sherman

Founding Director

As a dear friend and brother in Christ to Shaun, Dan deeply understands and embraces the significance of establishing the Shaun Duvall Legacy Foundation. As a Founding Director, he is passionate about advancing the Foundation's mission to make a lasting impact through community and selfless acts of service that create meaningful opportunities for others.

Professionally, Dan brings more than 30 years of experience in technology, executive leadership, consulting, and organizational development across both for-profit and nonprofit organizations. He currently serves as Chief Technology Officer at Moneta and as an Adjunct Professor in the Master of Engineering program at Washington University in St. Louis. Throughout his career, Dan has held numerous consulting and advisory roles and has founded two companies.

Beyond his professional accomplishments, Dan's relationship with Shaun was rooted in a deep friendship, shared faith, and a genuine commitment to serving others. It is this personal connection, combined with his professional experience and passion for making a difference, that makes Dan honored to serve as a Founding Director of the Shaun Duvall Legacy Foundation.

Mission & Programs

Investing in the Next Generation of Servant Leaders

Our mission, values, and the programs we're building to carry it out.

Our Mission

To glorify God by investing in and developing the next generation of servant leaders and entrepreneurs.

Through financial support, mentorship, meaningful relationships, service, and connection, we champion young people who need someone to believe in their potential, help them discover and pursue their purpose, and equip them to lead by example, serve others, and multiply their impact.

Our Vision

A Growing Community of Servant Leaders

To build a growing community of servant leaders who use their gifts, relationships, and influence to serve others, create opportunity, and invest in the generation coming behind them — multiplying positive impact from one life to another. We are building a community, not simply a scholarship fund.

Our Programs

The Shaun Duvall Legacy Scholars Program

Two paths. One Legacy Year. One purpose. Each year, the Foundation intends to select two emerging leaders — one Legacy Education Scholar and one Legacy Entrepreneur Fellow. Both receive financial investment and enter the same 12-month Legacy Year together. The money opens the door; the relational investment is the heart of the program.

🎓

Legacy Education Scholar

A graduating high-school senior pursuing an approved postsecondary path: college, community college, trade or technical school, apprenticeship, certification, or another legitimate career-training pathway.

💼

Legacy Entrepreneur Fellow

An emerging entrepreneur under 30 with a defined business concept, written business plan, and meaningful early steps toward launch — beyond the idea stage, but still early enough for Foundation investment to matter.

Both paths are open to applicants who live within the Foundation's local service area, initially envisioned as roughly a 45-minute drivable radius. The Foundation is openly Christian; recipients are not required to identify as Christian.

The Program

The 12-Month Legacy Year

Receiving an award is the beginning, not the conclusion. Each Scholar and Fellow commits to a year built around relationship, growth, service, and multiplication.

1

Begin With Their Story

Foundation leadership meets each recipient to understand their story, why, and goals.

2

Coffee & Leadership

Six 1:1 conversations with six mentors, selected intentionally for that person.

3

Foundation Check-Ins

Informal relationship conversations at the beginning, middle, and end of the year.

4

Serve Together

One required community-service project, served alongside the Foundation.

5

Represent the Foundation

Recipients advocate for and represent the Foundation when reasonably able.

6

Return to the Gala

Recipients return the following year for a live Q&A and to welcome the incoming class.

In-Kind Gala Partnerships

Support the Gala With a Contribution, Not Cash

The Foundation may accept selected products, experiences, artwork, or services in place of a cash sponsorship when the contribution can meaningfully support the Gala, reduce an event expense, or generate fundraising revenue.

Supporting In-Kind Partner
$500–$999 contributed value
  • 2 Gala tickets
  • Legacy of Love Gala gift for each guest
  • Supporting In-Kind Partner recognition
  • Business name/logo recognition in Gala materials
  • Recognition connected to the donated auction item or experience
  • Foundation website and event communication recognition
  • Pre-Gala social media recognition
  • Post-Gala sponsor thank-you recognition
Premier In-Kind Gala Partner
$1,000–$1,999 contributed value
  • 4 Gala tickets
  • VIP seating
  • Upgraded personalized Gala gift for each guest
  • Premier In-Kind Gala Partner recognition
  • Business name/logo recognition in Gala materials
  • Recognition connected to the donated auction item or experience
  • Foundation website and event communication recognition
  • Pre-Gala social media recognition
  • Post-Gala sponsor thank-you recognition

In-kind contributions of $2,000+: exceptional high-value gifts will be reviewed individually so recognition and benefits can be tailored appropriately without automatically mirroring a cash sponsorship.

Examples of contributions we may consider: artwork, jewelry, vacation stays, experiences, professional services needed for the Gala, auction packages, and other goods or services specifically approved by the Foundation.

Why in-kind partnerships are structured separately: In-kind gifts help create meaningful fundraising value while allowing the Foundation to preserve cash-sponsorship and ticket revenue. Recognition and benefits are based on the accepted contributed value and are separate from cash sponsorship levels.
A note for auction & art partners: for donated artwork, jewelry, or other auction pieces, the Foundation will review the proposed contribution for auction appeal and fundraising potential. Partners should provide a description of the item, artist/business information, and customary selling or retail information when available. Final acceptance and placement are at the Foundation's discretion.
Formation & tax notice: The Shaun Duvall Legacy Foundation is currently in the formation and federal tax-exemption application process. The Foundation does not currently represent or guarantee that any payment or contribution is tax-deductible. Because Gala tickets, gifts, and sponsorship arrangements provide goods or services in return, any potentially deductible amount may be reduced by the fair market value of benefits received. Donors should consult their own tax adviser. In-kind donors are responsible for substantiating the value they claim for donated property.
